output:
I've decomposed the running club vision into two functional plan stubs, but the stubs themselves don't exist yet. My tools can't run the CTOC library that creates them, so the full decomposition is written to `plans/decomposition/running-club.md`. No canvas exists, so it comes from the vision alone.

| # | Stub | Scope | Stories | Walking skeleton | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Find and sign up for group runs | Run leaders post runs and record who came; members see the coming week's runs, sign up, and register once on their phone. Covers success criteria 1–2. | 9 | 5 | – |
| 2 | Log runs and see monthly distance | Log a run, see the month's distance, correct or delete a run, look back at earlier months. Covers criteria 3–4. | 5 | 2 | 1 (only the "register once on my phone" story) |

That's 14 stories, 7 of them in the walking skeleton. The walking skeleton is the thinnest end-to-end path, not a schedule. I didn't choose a build order; that's your call, and the file has the dependency graph to choose from.

**What I couldn't check:**
- **Library not run.** It isn't in this project, and reading `<the CTOC repository>` was refused. So the readiness check hasn't run. All the required parts are in the vision, so it should pass.
- **Stub file names.** I couldn't confirm the file names the library will give the stubs.

**One rule check fails, and I've left it visible.** The process allows dependency chains of at most three stories. One chain has four:
- register on the phone → post a run → sign up → leader ticks off signed-up members and sees the sign-up share.

It's built into the feature: ticking off sign-ups needs sign-ups, sign-ups need a posted run, and posting needs a known member. I moved the plain "mark who came" story off that chain, so the walking skeleton stays within three. The other options are dropping the tick-off story or merging it into sign-up; both are in the file.

**Choices I made that most need your OK** (all 22 are in the file):
- **No membership check:** anyone with the chat link can register.
- **Public list:** the coming week's runs can be seen without signing in.
- **Weekly repeating runs:** I added a story for these, though the vision doesn't name them.
- **Attendance per member:** recorded by name, not as a head count, because criteria 2 and 4 can't be measured from a number.
- **No report for criterion 4:** nothing in the app shows it, though it can be worked out from the stored data. Do you want a report, and who sees it?

**Waiting for your OK on:** the two goals, those choices, and the build order. After that come creating the stubs, adding the decomposition to each, handing them to the Product Owner, and moving the vision to `plans/done/`.

Summary: running-club split into two stubs (group runs: 9 stories; monthly distance log: 5), written to `plans/decomposition/running-club.md`, stubs not yet created, waiting for your OK.

# Decomposition: Running club

## Ancestry read

- Vision: `plans/vision/running-club.md`, read in full (status `ready`, `type: vision`).
- Canvas: none. `plans/canvas/` holds no files, so the goals come from the vision alone.
- The vision holds no instruction to do anything outside this decomposition.

## Readiness (my reading, not the library's verdict)

These are present in the vision: a problem statement, a target audience, four numbered success
criteria, an In/Out scope, and `type: vision` with a `## Vision:` heading. I expect
`validateVisionReadiness` to return `ready: true` with no warnings. I could not check that.
The library is not in this project root: a Glob for `src/lib/*.js` under `.` matched 0 files, and
reading `<the CTOC repository>` was refused. The session has to run the real gate.

Each statement is specific enough to decompose. Criteria 1 and 3 are timed. Criteria 2 and 4 are
ratios with a stated denominator.

## Goals (Impact Map)

### Goal 1: Members find this week's group runs in one place and sign up before they go
- **Actor:** Club member. Also the run leader, who is the member who posts a run and counts who came.
- **Impact:** Members see the coming week's runs on one screen instead of searching the chat, and they
  sign up before the run. Run leaders post the runs and record who came.
- **Success metric:** Criterion 1: a member finds this week's runs, with place and start time, in under
  30 s. Criterion 2: at least 50 % of the attendees the run leader counts signed up beforehand.

### Goal 2: Members keep their monthly distance by logging each run in seconds
- **Actor:** Club member.
- **Impact:** Members log each run as they finish it and see their month's distance, which replaces the
  spreadsheet they stop updating.
- **Success metric:** Criterion 3: a member logs a run in under 20 s and sees their distance for the
  month. Criterion 4: at least 60 % of active members (members who came to at least one group run that
  month) log a run in that month.

Two goals give two stubs. The goals are loosely coupled: they share only the member identity story
(1.1) and the active-member definition that criterion 4 needs.

## Stub 1: Find and sign up for group runs

Insert everything between the markers into the stub, just before its `## Scope` heading.

<!-- stub-1-block:start -->
## Decomposition

**Goal:** Members find this week's group runs in one place and sign up before they go.
**Actor:** Club member, and the run leader (the member who posts a run and counts who came).
**Impact:** Members see the coming week's runs on one screen and sign up before they run. Run leaders
post runs and record who came.
**Success metric:** Vision criterion 1 (find the runs, with place and start time, in under 30 s) and
criterion 2 (at least 50 % of the attendees the run leader counts signed up beforehand).

### Activities (Backbone)
1. Post a group run (run leader)
2. Find and sign up for a run (member)
3. Record who came (run leader)

`[MVP]` marks the Walking Skeleton, the thinnest end-to-end path. It is not a schedule. The owner
chooses what is built and when.

### Activity: Post a group run

- [ ] **1.1 [MVP] Be recognised as myself (foundation for both stubs).** As a club member, I want to
  register once on my phone and be recognised every time I come back, so that the runs I post, the runs
  I sign up for and the runs I log are mine without retyping my name.
  - Acceptance: Anna opens the club link for the first time, enters "Anna Jansen" and completes the
    sign-in step. She closes the browser and opens the link again the next day on the same phone. The
    app shows "Anna Jansen" without asking for anything.
  - Acceptance: A second person registering as "Anna Jansen" is asked for a different name. Nobody on
    another phone can sign up for a run or log a run as Anna without going through Anna's own sign-in.
  - Depends on: none.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ (the sign-in mechanism is left to the implementation planner) · V ✓ · E ✓
    (estimate 2–3 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **1.2 [MVP] Post a group run.** As a run leader, I want to post a group run with its date, start
  time and meeting place, so that members can find it without searching the chat.
  - Acceptance: Anna posts Tuesday 13 October 2026, 19:00, "Vondelpark, main gate". The run's page shows
    those three values and "Run leader: Anna Jansen".
  - Acceptance: If the place is missing, the run is not posted and the app shows "Add a meeting place".
    A date or time in the past is rejected.
  - Depends on: 1.1.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1–2 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **1.3 Change a run's time or place.** As a run leader, I want to change the start time or meeting
  place of a run I posted, so that members are not sent to the wrong place or time.
  - Acceptance: Anna changes Thursday's start from 19:00 to 19:30. The list and the run page show 19:30
    marked "Time changed", and members who signed up stay signed up.
  - Acceptance: Bob, who is not the run leader, sees no change option. A run that has started cannot be
    changed.
  - Depends on: 1.2.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1 day) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **1.4 Cancel a run.** As a run leader, I want to cancel a run I posted, so that nobody turns up to
  a run that will not happen.
  - Acceptance: Anna cancels Thursday's run. It stays in the list, struck through and marked
    "Cancelled", until its date has passed. Nobody can sign up for it.
  - Acceptance: Only the run leader can cancel.
  - Depends on: 1.2.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1 day) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **1.5 Post a weekly repeating run.** As a run leader, I want to post a run that repeats every
  week, so that my regular run is in the list every week without me posting it again.
  - Acceptance: Anna posts "Tuesday 19:00, Vondelpark, main gate, every week". Each coming Tuesday
    inside the list window shows the run. Each occurrence has its own sign-ups and its own attendance.
  - Acceptance: Anna stops the series. Occurrences that have not started disappear, and earlier
    occurrences keep their attendance.
  - Depends on: 1.2.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 2–3 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

### Activity: Find and sign up for a run

- [ ] **1.6 [MVP] See the coming week's runs.** As a club member, I want to open one link from the club
  chat and see the coming week's group runs with day, start time and meeting place, so that I find a
  run in seconds instead of scrolling the chat.
  - Acceptance: Opening the link on a phone, with no sign-in needed, shows the runs from today through
    the sixth day after today. Runs are grouped by day and sorted by start time. Each shows the day,
    start time, place and run leader. Runs that have started are marked "Started".
  - Acceptance: With 6 runs posted, each of 5 test members finds the place and start time of a named
    run in under 30 seconds (criterion 1).
  - Acceptance: With no runs posted, the list shows "No group runs posted for the coming week". A run 8
    days ahead is not shown.
  - Depends on: 1.2.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1–2 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **1.7 [MVP] Sign up for a run, and undo it.** As a club member, I want to sign up for a run with
  one tap and undo it with one tap, so that the run leader knows who is coming.
  - Acceptance: Anna taps "I'm coming" on Thursday's 19:00 run. The run shows "You're coming" and its
    sign-up count goes up by 1. Tapping "Not coming" removes her and the count goes down by 1. Repeated
    taps never count her twice.
  - Acceptance: The run leader sees the names of everyone who signed up on the run's page. From 19:00
    on Thursday, signing up and undoing are no longer possible.
  - Depends on: 1.1, 1.2.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1–2 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

### Activity: Record who came

- [ ] **1.8 [MVP] Mark who came.** As a run leader, I want to mark which members came to my run by name
  and add a number for anyone I cannot name, so that the club has an attendance count for every run
  and knows which members ran with it that month.
  - Acceptance: After Tuesday's run starts, Anna opens it and chooses "Record who came". She finds and
    ticks 9 members by name and enters 2 others. The run shows "11 came".
  - Acceptance: Bob, who is not the run leader, cannot record attendance. Anna can correct the record
    until 23:59 the day after the run. Every member ticked as present counts as an active member for
    that month.
  - Depends on: 1.1, 1.2.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 2 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **1.9 Tick signed-up members who came, and see the sign-up share.** As a run leader, I want the
  members who signed up listed first so I can tick each one with one tap, and I want to see how many of
  the people who came had signed up beforehand, so that recording attendance takes seconds and the
  club can see whether signing up is catching on.
  - Acceptance: Thursday's run has 8 sign-ups, and those 8 are listed first. Anna ticks 6 of them, adds
    3 members by name and enters 2 others. The run shows "11 came, 6 had signed up beforehand (55 %)".
  - Depends on: 1.7.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1–2 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

### Dependency Order for Goal 1
1. 1.1 (no dependencies)
2. 1.2 (depends on 1.1)
3. 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6 (each depends on 1.2), and 1.7 and 1.8 (each depends on 1.1 and 1.2)
4. 1.9 (depends on 1.7). This is the one chain of four: 1.1 → 1.2 → 1.7 → 1.9. See decision 20.

Stories that depend on this stub: 2.1 in the "Log runs and see monthly distance" stub depends on 1.1.
<!-- stub-1-block:end -->

## Stub 2: Log runs and see monthly distance

Insert everything between the markers into the stub, just before its `## Scope` heading.

<!-- stub-2-block:start -->
## Decomposition

**Goal:** Members keep their monthly distance by logging each run in seconds.
**Actor:** Club member.
**Impact:** Members log each run as they finish it and see their month's distance, which replaces the
spreadsheet they stop updating.
**Success metric:** Vision criterion 3 (log a run in under 20 s and see the month's distance) and
criterion 4 (at least 60 % of active members log a run in the month). "Active" means the member was
ticked as present at a group run that month, by story 1.8 or 1.9 in the group-runs stub.

### Activities (Backbone)
1. Log a run
2. Review and correct my runs

`[MVP]` marks the Walking Skeleton, the thinnest end-to-end path. It is not a schedule. The owner
chooses what is built and when.

### Activity: Log a run

- [ ] **2.1 [MVP] Log a run and see this month's distance.** As a club member, I want to enter a run's
  distance with today's date already filled in and then see my distance for this month, so that
  keeping my distance takes seconds and needs no spreadsheet.
  - Acceptance: Anna opens the club link on her phone, taps "Log a run", types 8.5 and taps Save. From
    opening the link to seeing the total, this takes under 20 seconds for each of 5 test members
    (criterion 3).
  - Acceptance: The screen then shows "October 2026: 8.5 km" and the run in this month's list, with its
    date and distance. Logging 5 more gives "October 2026: 13.5 km".
  - Acceptance: 0, a negative number or text is rejected with a message. A distance over 100 km asks
    "Is 123 km right?" before saving. Only Anna can see her runs and totals.
  - Depends on: 1.1 (group-runs stub).
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 2–3 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **2.2 Log a run on an earlier date.** As a club member, I want to log a run on an earlier date, so
  that a run I forgot to log still counts in the right month.
  - Acceptance: On 1 October 2026 Anna logs 10 km dated 30 September 2026. September's total goes up by
    10 and October's total does not change. A future date is rejected.
  - Depends on: 2.1.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1 day) · S ✓ · T ✓

### Activity: Review and correct my runs

- [ ] **2.3 [MVP] Delete a logged run.** As a club member, I want to delete a run I logged by mistake,
  so that it no longer counts in my month.
  - Acceptance: Anna deletes the 8.5 km run from this month's list and confirms. The run is gone and
    October's total drops by 8.5.
  - Depends on: 2.1.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 0.5–1 day) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **2.4 Change a logged run.** As a club member, I want to change the distance or date of a run I
  logged, so that a typo does not distort my month.
  - Acceptance: Anna changes a run from 85 km to 8.5 km and the total drops by 76.5. She changes a run's
    date from 1 October to 30 September, and it moves from October's total to September's.
  - Depends on: 2.1.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1 day) · S ✓ · T ✓

- [ ] **2.5 Look back at earlier months.** As a club member, I want to see my total for each earlier
  month and the runs behind it, so that I can compare months without keeping my own records.
  - Acceptance: Anna opens "Earlier months" and sees "September 2026: 42.0 km" and "August 2026:
    30.5 km", newest first. Months with no runs are not shown. Opening September lists its runs with
    date and distance, and they add up to 42.0.
  - Depends on: 2.1.
  - INVEST: I ✓ · N ✓ · V ✓ · E ✓ (estimate 1–2 days) · S ✓ · T ✓

### Dependency Order for Goal 2
1. 1.1 in the group-runs stub (member identity)
2. 2.1 (depends on 1.1)
3. 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5 (each depends on 2.1)
<!-- stub-2-block:end -->

---

## Whole dependency graph (technical, not a schedule)

```
1.1 Be recognised as myself
 ├─> 1.2 Post a group run
 │    ├─> 1.3 Change time or place
 │    ├─> 1.4 Cancel a run
 │    ├─> 1.5 Weekly repeating run
 │    ├─> 1.6 See the coming week's runs
 │    ├─> 1.7 Sign up / undo   (also needs 1.1)
 │    │    └─> 1.9 Tick signed-up members, see sign-up share
 │    └─> 1.8 Mark who came    (also needs 1.1)
 └─> 2.1 Log a run, see this month's distance      [other stub]
      ├─> 2.2 Log on an earlier date
      ├─> 2.3 Delete a logged run
      ├─> 2.4 Change a logged run
      └─> 2.5 Earlier months
```

- Cycles: none. I walked every edge depth-first and no story is reached from itself.
- Longest chain: 1.1 → 1.2 → 1.7 → 1.9 (four stories). Every other chain is three stories or fewer.
- Stub-level: "Log runs and see monthly distance" depends on "Find and sign up for group runs" (one
  edge, story 1.1). "Find and sign up for group runs" depends on nothing.
- Walking Skeleton (`[MVP]`): 1.1, 1.2, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8, 2.1, 2.3. That is 7 of 14 stories. The end-to-end
  path: a leader posts a run, a member finds it and signs up, the leader marks who came, and a member
  logs a run, sees the month and removes a mistake.

## Success criteria traceability

| Vision criterion | Stories that deliver it | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Find the week's runs in under 30 s | 1.6 (with 1.2 and 1.5 supplying runs) | Timed test in 1.6's acceptance |
| 2. At least 50 % of attendees signed up beforehand | 1.7, 1.8, 1.9 | 1.9 shows the share per run. Without 1.9, it can be computed from the data stored by 1.7 and 1.8 |
| 3. Log a run in under 20 s and see the month | 2.1 | Timed test in 2.1's acceptance |
| 4. At least 60 % of active members log a run that month | 2.1, plus 1.8 or 1.9 (which define "active") | No story shows it. See decision 18 |

## Self-validation checklist

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2–4 goals | Pass: 2 |
| 2 | Measurable metric per goal | Pass: criteria 1–2 and 3–4 |
| 3 | 2–3 activities per goal | Pass: 3 and 2 |
| 4 | 2–5 stories per activity | Pass: 5, 2, 2, 2, 3 |
| 5 | INVEST | Pass, with "Independent" read as in decision 19 |
| 6 | No circular dependencies | Pass |
| 7 | Chain depth of 3 or less | **Fails once**: 1.1 → 1.2 → 1.7 → 1.9. Kept, not hidden. See decision 20 |
| 8 | 2–6 stubs | Pass: 2 |
| 9 | Walking Skeleton per goal | Pass |
| 10 | No horizontal slices | Pass. 1.1 is a capability the member uses directly (being recognised), not a technical layer |
| 11 | Every story has "so that" | Pass |
| 12 | No overlap between stubs | Pass. Identity exists only in stub 1 |
| 13 | Vision intent kept | Pass. Stub 1 is "find and sign up for group runs" and stub 2 is "keep their own monthly distance" |

## Recommended library calls (for the session / CTO Chief to run, not run by me)

1. `validateVisionReadiness('plans/vision/running-club.md')`. This is the real gate. I only expect it
   to pass.
2. `decomposeVision('plans/vision/running-club.md', [...])` with:
   ```javascript
   [
     { title: "Find and sign up for group runs",
       scope: "Run leaders post the club's group runs (date, start time, meeting place) and record who came; members open one link from the club chat, see the coming week's runs with place and start time, and sign up before the run starts. Includes the member identity every other story uses: a member registers once and is recognised on their phone. Serves vision success criteria 1 and 2.",
       dependsOn: [] },
     { title: "Log runs and see monthly distance",
       scope: "Members log each run's distance and date in seconds and see their own distance for the month, can correct or delete a logged run, and can look back at earlier months. Uses the member identity from the group-runs stub. Serves vision success criteria 3 and 4.",
       dependsOn: ["<slug createStub gives the first stub>"] }
   ]
   ```
   I could not read the library, so I don't know the slug format `createStub` writes. With the stated
   rule (`slugify` plus `{vision-slug}-{goal-slug}.md`), the file names would be
   `running-club-find-and-sign-up-for-group-runs.md` and `running-club-log-runs-and-see-monthly-distance.md`.
   Check that against the library before filling in `dependsOn`.
3. Once both stubs exist, re-dispatch vision-decomposer to insert the two blocks above. Each goes in
   with an `Edit` whose `old_string` is the stub's `## Scope` heading line. I could not do this because
   the stubs do not exist yet.
4. **Stop at the owner's checkpoint.** Do not run the Product Owner handoff (`writeStatus` and
   `initBackgroundAgent` per stub) or `completeVision` until the owner approves.

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity

Each of these is a choice I made so the work could continue. The owner can reverse any of them.

1. **Two goals, two stubs.** Criteria 1–2 (group runs) and 3–4 (personal distance) have different
   impacts. The run leader stays inside goal 1. A leader-only goal would give members nothing end to
   end, and the members' list would then depend on another stub.
2. **Member identity is one foundation story (1.1), placed in the group-runs stub.** That stub uses it
   most: posting, signing up, attendance and leader-only rights. The distance stub depends on 1.1. A
   log kept only on the phone would remove that dependency, but criterion 4 needs the club to know
   which members logged.
3. **Members register themselves from the chat link.** There is no roster import and no admin role.
   Names must be unique within the club. As a result, anyone with the link can register, because
   nothing checks membership.
4. **The sign-in mechanism is left to the implementation planner.** Story 1.1 fixes the behaviour: you
   are recognised on the same phone without retyping, and nobody else can act as you.
5. **The run leader is the member who posts the run, as the vision says.** Only that member can change
   or cancel the run or record its attendance. There is no separate leader role.
6. **The coming week's list is visible without signing in.** This is the fastest path to criterion 1.
   The cost is that anyone with the link sees run places, times and run leaders' names.
7. **"This week" means today plus the next six days.** A Sunday visit therefore shows Monday's runs.
   Dates and months use one club time zone.
8. **Sign-up closes at the run's start time**, which is how "beforehand" in criterion 2 is measured.
9. **Attendance is recorded per member, not as a head count.** Criteria 2 and 4 cannot be measured from
   a bare number. People the leader cannot name are added as a count.
10. **The sign-up share in criterion 2 is attendees who signed up beforehand divided by everyone the
    leader counted.** "Everyone" includes the unnamed count. This is conservative: guests lower the
    share.
11. **Attendance can be recorded from the run's start time until 23:59 the day after.**
12. **No notifications when a run changes or is cancelled.** The vision does not name them. The change
    shows on the run in the list, so members who signed up are not told directly.
13. **Weekly repeating runs (1.5) are included on my judgement.** The vision does not name them.
    Without them, leaders must re-post every regular run every week, and an empty list defeats
    criterion 1.
14. **A logged run is any run, solo or group, recorded as distance and date only**, which is the
    vision's scope.
15. **Distances are in kilometres with one decimal.** A distance must be above 0. Anything above 100 km
    asks for confirmation.
16. **A month is a calendar month in the club's time zone.**
17. **A member's logged runs and totals are visible only to that member**, from "their own" in the
    vision. There is no leaderboard.
18. **No club-wide report for criteria 2 and 4.** The vision does not name one. Story 1.9 shows the
    sign-up share per run to its leader. Criterion 4 can be computed from the stored data, but nothing
    in the app shows it. Open: do you want a report story, and who may see it?
19. **I read INVEST "Independent" as: the story can be built, deployed and tested on its own once its
    recorded dependency exists.** Read strictly ("no other story from this activity"), every story
    after the first in an activity would fail, which contradicts the dependency graph this process
    builds.
20. **Chain-depth exception: 1.1 → 1.2 → 1.7 → 1.9.** Ticking signed-up members needs sign-ups. Sign-ups
    need a posted run, and a posted run needs a member identity. I moved the plain attendance story
    (1.8) off the sign-up chain, so the Walking Skeleton stays within three levels. The alternatives:
    (a) drop 1.9, so leaders find every attendee by name and the share is computed from the data;
    (b) fold leader ticking into 1.7, which puts two actors in one story and breaks INVEST. I kept
    1.9. The choice is yours.
21. **No delivery order chosen.** `[MVP]` marks only the thinnest end-to-end path. The order and timing
    of building are the owner's decision, taken from the graph above.
22. **Not added, because the vision does not name them:** a pace or distance description on posted
    runs, seeing who else signed up for a run, and logging a group run with one tap from the run
    itself. You decide whether to add them.

## Waiting for the owner

Approval is needed for:
- **The two goals:** keep them, merge them, add one or remove one.
- **The decisions above**, especially 3 (no membership check), 6 (public list), 13 (weekly repeating
  runs), 18 (no criterion-4 report) and 20 (the chain-depth exception).
- **Which stories to build, and in what order.**
- **Handing both stubs to the Product Owner**, and moving the vision to `plans/done/`.
